overall: The AG found violations for the July 18 executive session missing from the notice, insufficient executive session detail, and inaccurate July 11 and July 18 minutes. It found no violation on purpose, the July 25 topics, or public comment, and declined the May 2 and other procedural claims.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged similar executive session and notice violations at the May 2 meeting, which the AG found untimely under the 30-day filing rule.
allegations.key_passage: We find the allegations regarding the May 2 meeting to be untimely and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 11 executive session was held though no executive session topic was listed on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Although we find that the July 11 executive session was unanticipated and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law, we remind the Commission that in those circumstances, public bodies are encouraged to postpone discussion of such topics until proper notice can be given to the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 18 executive sessions were held though neither was listed on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by pursuing two separate executive sessions on this topic at the July 18 meeting even though they were not listed on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the reasons given for the July 11 and July 18 executive sessions were not valid.
allegations.key_passage: we conclude that the discussions that were held in executive session on July 11 and July 18 fell within executive session Purpose 3, as they constituted a discussion of imminently threatened litigation against the County.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session topics for July 11 and July 18 were not described with enough detail to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide sufficient detail about the specific topic in its open session statement as well as the notice for the July 18 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the July 18 minutes were inaccurate because they omitted the Chief Information Officer's presence and comments; the AG also reviewed the July 11 minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We agree that the Commission omitted entire discussions from both the July 11 and July 18 meeting minutes

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes omitted non-member officials, the minutes-taker was absent for part of a session, and the executive session votes were not seconded.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, none of these allegations would constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged two July 25 notice topics, the County Owned Buildings Policy and IT Reorganization, lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: The topics as listed included sufficient detail to inform the public of the anticipated discussion and indeed adequately described the discussion that actually took place during the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission did not allow public comment on the July 25 topics.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law by declining to allow public comment.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Revise the July 11 and July 18 open session minutes to accurately reflect the discussions that took place at the meetings, within 30 days
Release the July 11 and July 18 executive session minutes within 30 days, unless a Public Records Law or attorney-client privilege exemption applies
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
